0.0.n: This word is borrowed from English and written in katakana.

0.1.n: で marks where the shopping takes place.

0.2.n: は makes the supermarket setting the topic of the sentence.

0.3.n: With で, this describes the group doing the shopping together.

0.4.n: で marks the group participating in the activity, rather than its location.

0.5.n: This noun combines with をする to describe the activity.

0.6.n: を links 買い物 to します, forming the expression for doing shopping.

0.7.n: します is the polite form of する; 買い物をします means to shop.

1.0.n: お and さん make this a familiar, respectful way to refer to a mother.

1.1.n: が identifies the mother as the person choosing the items.

1.2.n: This refers to merchandise, not just any objects.

1.3.n: を marks 商品 as what the mother chooses.

1.4.n: 選んで is the て-form of 選ぶ, connecting this action to the next part of the sentence.

2.0.n: お and さん make this a familiar, respectful way to refer to a father.

2.1.n: は sets the father as the topic, contrasting his role with the mother's.

2.2.n: This refers to the shopping load being carried, rather than necessarily travel luggage.

2.3.n: を marks 荷物 as what the father carries.

2.4.n: 持ちます is the polite form of 持つ, which can mean hold or carry.

3.0.n: Adding たち makes this explicitly refer to more than one child.

3.1.n: たち attaches to 子供 to indicate a group of children.

3.2.n: は marks the children as the topic of this sentence.

3.3.n: This snack name is borrowed from English and written in katakana.

3.4.n: や lists examples without suggesting that these are the only things bought.

3.5.n: This English loanword is written in katakana.

3.6.n: を marks the whole list of snacks as what the children buy.

3.7.n: 買います is the polite form of 買う, describing what the children do.

0.lit: At the supermarket, as a family, shopping do.
0.tip: The first で marks the location; the second で marks the group acting together.

1.tip: 選んで connects to the following clause, so the sentence continues even though the next person is different.

2.lit: As for the father, bags carries.
2.tip: は shifts the topic to the father and what he does.

3.lit: As for the children, potato chips and chocolate, among other things, buy.
3.tip: や gives examples of purchases rather than a complete list.
